The Eye's second half. §9Sirius B§r (T5) cools white dwarfs into black ones, and §9the magnetar§r (T6) runs on Antipolarization Agent. The §9Quasar Engine§r and the first galaxies (T7, T8) are here: the quasar's bursts hold the Eye together and power your base.

The bottom rows hold the pack's own UXV parts and machines. The crafted Stargate now waits in §1The Endgame§r, after MAX.

The last voltage tier. Eye T9 holds the §9Great Attractor§r on a beam of pellets and makes §9Attractor Dark Matter§r; every MAX part is built from it. The Homogeny T3 and the two Reality machines make the §9Universal Upgrade Core§r, and Eye T10 runs §9the Universe§r: the only Universium, which opens §1The Endgame§r.

Eye T10's Universium opens this tab: the pack's MHDCSM line, Constrained Eternity and Resplendent parts, the crafted Stargate and the Astral Array. The Supermassive Lattice's last tiers sit here too: L3 (on Universium), L4, Overdrive and Unbound.

§1GTNH: Beyond the Stars - the nuclear campus.§r

One controller, one projection, and every inlet cut into the building it feeds. The top two rows are a §9ten-step beginner path§r: craft the controller, break ground, project the plant, plumb the points of use, load the rods, first steam, seat the rotors, wire the clock, first EU, read the panel.

The third row is the deep end - laser output, spin doctrine, the propellant and coolant ladders, and the safety sheet. The two fluid ladders open at step 7, one step before the clock, because a chamber with no propellant and no coolant refuses every cycle and the plant never spins. The two middle rows are bills of materials; those do not count toward completion.

§1The row under the blueprints is THE CAMPAIGN§r - and it is where the ten-step path leads. Finishing the build is the beginning, not the end: four milestone lines climb just by running the plant, and the points they pay buy a twenty-five node upgrade tree on the Nuclear Plant Foundation.

The last row is §1The Fuel Line§r: every rod this plant burns, from ore to bundle.

§8Ten steps, in order, and you are making power. You do not need to know anything about this plant to start.§r

§1§lWHAT §lIT §lIS§r
One nuclear campus raised by ONE hologram projection: a 50x50 platform, a reactor silo fed by falling fuel rods, a 3x3 turbine spine, a 7x7 injection chamber and a rotor gallery. A fully tuned tier-5 plant pushes toward a billion EU/t.

§5§lDO §lTHIS§r
Assemble the §9Nuclear Plant Foundation§r in an Assembling Machine (IV, 60 s, programmed circuit 4):
  1x Radiation Proof Machine Casing
  4x IV Circuit
  2x Lead Dense Plate
  8x Tungstensteel Plate
  8x Tungsten Rod
  2x Iridium Plate
  2x Rhodium-Plated Palladium Plate
  4 ingots of Molten Platinum

§2§lDONE §lWHEN§r
The controller is in your inventory. §8Nothing is taken from you - this quest only looks, and once it has seen the controller it stays complete for ever.§r
§8Claim the reward before step 2 plants that controller in the ground.§r

[note]This ONE machine is the whole plant. There are no module controllers: the cooling towers, the spine duct, the spiral chamber, the rotor gallery AND the four plant modules (Vent Stack, Switchyard, Extraction Derrick, Enrichment Annex) are all pieces of THIS controller, raised by the same projection.[/note]

§5§lDO §lTHIS§r
§91.§r Find flat ground with room. The platform is§9 50 x 50 blocks§r: it reaches 32 blocks BEHIND the controller and 17 in FRONT, with the controller about halfway across, and the plant wants 20 to 40 blocks of headroom depending on tier.

§92.§r Place the Nuclear Plant Foundation. §1Whichever way you are facing when you place it is the plant's FRONT§r - the silo grows straight back from it, and every socket you will ever pipe into faces the way you are facing now.

§93.§r Open its GUI. Three small unlabelled number fields sit at the bottom right, with a small square §9chart button§r to their left. Reading LEFT to RIGHT:
  §9Upgrade Tree§r - the BUTTON, not a field. Nothing to set yet; it opens the progression tree you will meet at the end of the path. Leave it alone for now.
  §9Build Tier§r - the NARROW field, 1-5: the silo size the projection raises. §1Start at 1.§r
  §9RPM Limit§r - the WIDEST field, 5 digits: the turbine redline you authorise. Leave it at 12,000.
  §9Control Rods§r - the field on the far right: rods N/24. Leave it at 24.
§8Hover any of the four to confirm which is which. All three fields already hold the value above, so changing nothing here is correct - and putting the tier in the rod field would run the whole campaign at 1/24 power.§r
§8The rod field will accept up to 36 and the RPM Limit up to 19,500, because the milestone lines and the upgrade tree can eventually withdraw the rods past the 24/24 design stop and lift the redline past 12,000. Until they do, anything above those two defaults is clamped straight back to them. Neither ever moves on its own: a tier raises the CEILING, and you type the value you want.§r

§2§lDONE §lWHEN§r
A §9Hologram Projector§r is in your inventory. §8Step 1 paid you one, and nothing is taken from you. That is the whole gate: a quest can only read what you are CARRYING, never what you have built.§r

§5§lCHECK §lYOUR §lWORK§r
The controller stands facing the way you want the plant to face, and §9Build Tier§r is set in its GUI. Neither of those is part of the gate above - but both have to be true before step 3 projects anything, and Build Tier can never be changed once a silo stands.

[warn]Choose the spot properly. Relocating a 50x50 plant later means breaking all of it. And Build Tier only decides what to RAISE: once a silo stands, the projection will never re-tier it - you would have to dismantle the silo first.[/warn]

§5§lDO §lTHIS§r
Right-click the controller with the §9Hologram Projector§r. The whole campus appears as a ghost, in this order:

  platform -> silo -> spine duct -> spiral chamber -> rotor assembly -> cooling tower, cooling tower -> vent stack -> switchyard -> extraction derrick -> enrichment annex

§2What the projection draws is exactly what the structure check wants.§r There is no build-only leniency left anywhere and no second controller to place. In survival the projector pulls blocks straight out of your inventory.

[img height=500]btsquests:textures/gui/plant-overview.png[/img]

§cWHAT THE PROJECTOR WILL NOT PLACE FOR YOU§r
It raises walls. It does not fit machines. When it has finished you still have to place, by hand:
 §9 12x Turbine Housing§r - 4 in the spine bore, 8 on the gallery centreline. Those cells are left as §cAIR§r,
     §8and they keep showing as ghosts for ever. That is the projector marking the spot, not a job it will finish.§r
  §9every hatch, injector, sensor and control block§r - those cells come out as §cPLAIN CASING§r. Break the casing, put the real machine in.
  §9the fuel pillars and rod loading ports§r inside the silo - optional interior, left as air.
Steps 4 to 9 place all of it, and every one of them hands you part of the bill.

§2§lDONE §lWHEN§r
You are holding the§9 64x Light Concrete§r and§9 16x Radiation Proof Machine Casing§r listed above. §8Steps 1 and 2 paid you exactly that. Claim this BEFORE you start projecting - in survival the projector eats blocks straight out of your pack as it works.§r

§5CHECK YOUR WORK - THE PROJECTION IS FINISHED WHEN§r
Right-clicking the controller with the projector places nothing more. The only cells still empty anywhere on the campus are then the§9 12 Turbine Housings§r and the silo interior.

§cThose 12 ghosts never go solid, and you have not done anything wrong.§r The hologram draws them and always will; the survival projector skips them every single time, on purpose, because a housing carries a spin setting and a rotor it has no business guessing. Step 7 places all twelve by hand. Do not stand there clicking at them.

§cThe controller is also still NOT FORMED at the end of this step.§r That is correct too. It is short of its §9Maintenance Hatch§r, its §9Feedwater Input Hatch§r, its §9Output Hatch§r and its §9Depleted Output Bus§r - four sockets, and step 4 fits all four along with the rest of the silo face and the chamber wall. §1The plant forms at the end of step 4, not here.§r

[note]Only the PLATFORM is mandatory. Silo, spine, spiral, gallery and towers are all optional pieces - but a platform on its own generates nothing, and a silo with no gallery is a steam EXPORT plant rather than a generator.[/note]

§1EVERY INLET SITS WHERE IT IS USED§r
There is no plumbing wall. Each insert and extract point is cut into the building it feeds, on the exact course it enters the plant's logic: rods go in at the fuel course they burn on, water at the drum, coolant and propellant at the chamber that spends them, power at the generator.

[img height=480]btsquests:textures/gui/point-of-use.png[/img]

§5THE SILO FACE - the flat wall your controller is set into§r
Three courses, one cell either side of the controller's own column - exactly as drawn above:
  §9y2§r  §9ROD§r Input Bus . §9DEP§r Depleted Output Bus
     §8two courses up: the lowest FUEL course, the exact segment the cascade burns§r
  §9y1§r  §9H2O§r Input Hatch . §9SILO CONTROL BLOCK§r . §9OUT§r Output Hatch
     §8the drum course - feedwater in, waste water and exported steam out§r
  §9y0§r  §9MAINT§r Maintenance Hatch, in the cell beside the controller

§5THE SPIRAL CHAMBER FRONT WALL - one course above the floor§r
  §9COOL§r Input Hatch - coolant, for the thing that actually overheats
  §9PROP§r Input Hatch - bulk propellant, directly under the eight injectors it stocks
  §9MNT§r Maintenance Hatch - the chamber carries its own, in the floor's front-right corner

§8The output manifold's own sockets - dynamos, energy and lasers - are step 9.§r

§5§lDO §lTHIS§r
Break the plain casing in each socket cell and place the machine there. Then run your logistics to each one; nothing is shared and nothing travels down a pipe you have to build.

§2§lDONE §lWHEN§r
All §9nine§r machines listed above are in your inventory at the same time.
§8This quest only LOOKS at what you are carrying, and it takes nothing. Hold the whole set at once, CLAIM it, and only then break the casings and set the machines into the wall. Already installed them? Wrench them back out for a moment - the check is on your inventory, not on the building.§r

§5§lCHECK §lYOUR §lWORK§r
Right-click the §9Silo Control Block§r you just set into the face. It prints the whole instrument panel, and the REACTOR group carries a §9Supply§r line reading§2 0 rods queued -> 0 pillar gaps§r.
§8Both zeros are right. A pillar gap is an empty segment in a §9Reactor Fuel Pillar Frame§r, and not one of those is standing yet. What this step pays you is§9 16 fuel-column BLOCKS§r - one block is one segment and 8 of them make a pillar, so that is§9 2 pillars§r - and they go up in step 5. Gaps appear when you raise the pillars; the queue moves when you feed the bus.§r
§1This is the step where the plant FORMS for the first time.§r §8Maintenance, Feedwater Input, Output Hatch and Depleted Output Bus are the only four sockets the structure actually demands, and they all just went in. Everything you fit from here on is added to a plant that is already alive.§r

[note]You never touch a rod port inside the silo again. The controller distributes rods from that one bus to all 45-201 pillars itself, every decay cycle - best grade first, lowest empty segment first.[/note]

§1THE DECAY CASCADE§r
Every fuel pillar is a gravity column 8 segments tall - 8 Reactor Fuel Pillar Frame blocks, stacked. A rod dropped in falls to the lowest empty segment. Only the §9BOTTOM§r one burns; when it is spent it drops into the depleted bus and the stack above shifts down one.

A pillar is §2LIVE§r while its bottom segment holds a burning rod:
  §9steam = live pillars x 16,384 L/t x fuel multiplier x rods N/24§r

§5§lTHE §lFUEL §lLADDER§r
  Uranium §8x1§r   MOX §8x2§r   Thorium-Bonded §8x5§r   Naquadah-Bonded §8x9§r
Same rod, same slot, nine times the steam at the top of the ladder.

§5§lDO §lTHIS§r
Feed fuel rods into the §9Rod Input Bus in the silo face§r - bottom fuel course, one cell to the LEFT of the controller §8as you stand outside and look at the silo§r - and keep it stocked. One rod is one segment, about 90 minutes, and a full pillar is roughly 12 hours.

§8You also need the pillars themselves: stacks of Reactor Fuel Pillar Frame blocks,§9 8 blocks to a pillar§r, standing inside the silo. The projector treats them as optional interior and leaves those cells empty, so a silo with no pillars makes no steam at all.§r

§2§lDONE §lWHEN§r
8 Uranium Fuel Rods are in your inventory. §8Claim it, then feed them to the bus - a rod inside the bus is inside a machine, not on you.§r

§5§lCHECK §lYOUR §lWORK§r
§1Do the arithmetic before you read the panel, so the number does not surprise you.§r Step 4 paid you§9 16 fuel-column BLOCKS§r and 8 blocks make one pillar, so what you are holding is§9 2 pillars§r - not 16. Stand them up as 2 stacks of 8, in 2 separate cells of the silo floor.
2 empty pillars are§9 16 empty segments§r, so the Supply line reads§2 0 rods queued -> 16 pillar gaps§r the moment they are up. Drop this step's 8 rods into the bus and it reads§2 8 rods queued -> 16 pillar gaps§r until the next decay cycle hands them out, then§2 0 rods queued -> 8 pillar gaps§r.
§cGaps with an EMPTY queue§r is the starving cascade, and that is the reading to act on;§2 0 gaps§r is a full silo. §8A tier-1 silo has room for 45 pillars - 360 blocks - so 2 is a start, not a finish. Blueprint: Reactor Silo has the count for every tier.§r

[warn]Classic fuel ASSEMBLIES in the bus still work, but at HALF output - the panel calls it "Assembly fallback (output halved)". The cascade is where the other half lives.[/warn]

[note]§1Where rods come from:§r §9The Fuel Line§r row at the bottom of this chapter - twenty-three steps, ore to bundle. §9Four pellets make a rod and three rods make a bundle.§r[/note]

§5§lDO §lTHIS§r
§91.§r Water into the silo face's §9H2O§r Input Hatch - the Input Hatch on the drum course, beside the Silo Control Block. §8Step 4 has the drawn map.§r
§92.§r Set Control Rods 1-24 in the GUI. Rods 24/24 is full power. §8A programmed circuit in the controller slot overrides the field.§r
§93.§r Enable the controller.

With no turbine chain behind it the plant simply §9exports Reactor Steam§r through the silo face's OUT hatch - or Hot Coolant, if you feed it IC2 Coolant instead of water. That is honest power, and it is a fraction of what this plant can do.

§cTHE REACTOR NEVER DRAWS EU§r
Nothing on the ten-step path needs to be powered. The plant generates; it does not consume - the reactor, the spine, the chamber and the gallery draw nothing at all, not idling, not starting, not running - and the four Energy Hatches in step 9 are §9not a structure requirement§r: this plant forms and runs perfectly well without a single one of them.

§1TWO THINGS ON THIS CAMPUS DO DRAW EU. BOTH ARE OPTIONAL MODULES.§r
The §9Extraction Derrick§r §2(1,920 EU/t§r) and the §9Enrichment Annex§r §2(480 EU/t§r) take their power §9through those same four Energy Hatches§r and from nowhere else. Build either one and the hatches stop being furniture: fit at least one and §9wire it to a live grid§r, or that module silently never turns over. Their blueprints are on the second blueprint row and both say so at the top.

§5§lREAD §lIT §lANYWHERE§r
The §9Silo Control Block§r prints the same instrument panel the GUI does. So does the Turbine Control Block, and so does a Portable Scanner. §8One panel, everywhere - no readout can disagree with another.§r

§2§lDONE §lWHEN§r
A §9Water Bucket§r is in your inventory. §8That is the whole gate - a quest reads your pack, not your plant. A bucket PRIMES the feedwater hatch; a reactor that is actually running wants a real water line behind it.§r

§5§lCHECK §lYOUR §lWORK§r
The REACTOR group shows live pillars and a non-zero §2L/t steam§r, and OUTPUT reads §2Steam export§r with a real number.

[note]Feedwater is NOT coolant. The hatch you just filled is the SILO's. The Spiral chamber has its own §9COOL§r hatch, on a different building, and neither can drink the other's fluid. §cStep 8 is where that one has to be fed§r - until it is, the turbine never leaves 0 RPM.[/note]

[warn]Every shutdown leaves DECAY HEAT: twenty minutes of mandatory cooling water. It is deferred, never waived. "Written in Fire" has the details.[/warn]

§1THE END OF THE PIPE§r
Steam leaves the silo down the spine duct, spirals through the injection chamber and blows through the §9ROTOR GALLERY§r. Eight stage housings sit on its centreline; four more sit in the spine bore.

§cPLACE ALL TWELVE YOURSELF§r
The projector deliberately skips every Turbine Housing cell - it leaves them as §cAIR§r, because a housing carries a spin setting and a rotor it has no business guessing. Craft twelve and place them:§9 4§r in the spine bore, filling every other cell starting one block out from the silo, and§9 8§r on the gallery centreline, again every other cell. The last of the eight hangs in the manifold mouth.

§5§lDO §lTHIS§r
§91.§r Right-click each of the eight gallery housings with a §9Turbine Rotor§r. Sneak-right-click empty-handed to pull one back out; the wear stays on the item.
§92.§r Right-click each of the four §9spine duct§r housings to set its spin - clockwise or anticlockwise. "Spin Doctrine" explains what that buys you; for now set all four the same and move on.

§5ROTORS WEAR, LIKE REAL BLADES§r
Each stage takes slow random damage at speed - roughly one point per ten minutes at full tilt. Every point costs that stage§c 5%§r, and at ten the rotor §cSHATTERS§r. The average factor over all eight sockets multiplies your whole output, so an empty socket is a 12.5% cut.

§1THE PLANT KEEPS RUNNING WHILE YOU DO THIS§r
Placing the eighth gallery housing does not stop the reactor and does not suddenly demand a hatch. It FORMS the Rotor Assembly, and one grey line appears in the OUTPUT group, opening §8Manifold: Energy Hatches 0/4§r and closing §8furniture, not a load; the plant runs without them§r. That is information, not a fault, and step 9 fills those sockets.
§cSkip them for ever only if you never build a plant module.§r The moment an §9Extraction Derrick§r or an §9Enrichment Annex§r stands on this campus, that same line stops saying furniture and starts reading §8the reactor never draws EU; the Derrick and the Annex do, through these§r - and with no hatch fitted at all it turns §cRED§r, because those two draw their EU through these sockets and will not run without one.

§1THE OUTPUT GROUP FLIPS ON THE FIRST ROTOR, NOT ON THE HOUSINGS§r
Twelve housings and no rotors still reads §2Steam export§r, because eight empty seats generate exactly nothing and the plant is genuinely still exporting steam out of the silo. The instant ONE rotor is seated it reads §2Generating§r instead. §8The MATH group re-titles itself on the same instant and for the same reason, so the two can never describe two different plants.§r

§2§lDONE §lWHEN§r
12 Turbine Housings and 8 Turbine Rotors are in your inventory at the same time. §8Step 6 paid you the twelve housings.§r
§8This step pays four Water Buckets as well as the injectors. They are not for the boiler - they are the first COOLANT for the Spiral chamber, and step 8 will not spin the fan without it.§r
§8This quest only LOOKS at what you are carrying, and it takes nothing. Hold the whole set at once, CLAIM it, and only then break the casings and set the machines into the wall. Already installed them? Wrench them back out for a moment - the check is on your inventory, not on the building.§r

§5§lCHECK §lYOUR §lWORK§r
The TURBINE group reads §2Rotors 8/8§r at an average factor near §2x1.00§r, and the STEAM CHAIN group shows§2 4 housings§r on the spine.

§1NOTHING HERE RUNS ON ITS OWN CLOCK - YOU SET THE PACE§r
A §9redstone rising edge§r on the TURBINE CONTROL BLOCK starts one CYCLE. A cycle drinks a buffered 20-tick slug of steam, opens a §9+/-2 tick window§r in which each of the eight injectors fires exactly 1 L of propellant, and adds RPM:

  §9gain = 176 x P x (timed / 8)§r

RPM bleeds off 0.5% every tick and the redline is§9 12,000§r. §cNo clock means the RPM decays to nothing, which means no EU at all.§r

§cAND A CYCLE IS REFUSED UNLESS THE CHAMBER IS PLUMBED§r
This is the step that catches people. Before a cycle is allowed to start, the plant checks two things about the Spiral chamber: that the injectors have propellant to fire, and that the §9COOLANT§r hatch can pay for the RPM that cycle would reach. If either answers no the cycle is §cREFUSED§r - no steam drunk, no propellant burned, no heat added, and §9no RPM§r.

§cSo a clock wired to a dry chamber leaves the whole plant at 0 EU/t for ever.§r It does not blow up and it does not break; it simply never spins, and the panel prints the reason on a §9HOLD:§r line. Both fluids go into the chamber's FRONT WALL, one course above the floor - §9COOL§r at one end, §9PROP§r at the other. Step 4 put those two hatches in. §1This step is where you fill them.§r

§2CLAIM THIS QUEST BEFORE YOU FIT ANY OF IT§r
Every machine named below goes INTO the plant, and this quest only reads what you are CARRYING. Hold the §9Turbine Control Block§r, the §9Spiral Cycle Sensor§r and all §9eight§r Precision Injectors at once, claim it, and only then start breaking casings. §8Already fitted some? Wrench them back out for a moment - the check is on your inventory, not on the building.§r

§cFIT THE EIGHT INJECTORS FIRST§r
The spiral chamber has eight §9Precision Injector§r sockets, one per interior level - world y 3 up to y 10 - each in the middle of one wall, walking round all four walls as the helix descends. The projector leaves every one of them as plain Tungstensteel Turbine Casing: break the casing and put the injector in its place.
§8Two of them stand 7 and 8 blocks above the platform. Bring scaffolding or fly.§r
The §9Spiral Cycle Sensor§r goes in the chamber ROOF, front-centre, facing UP.

§5THEN DO THIS, IN THIS ORDER§r
§91.§r Set the Turbine Control Block into the §9output manifold back face§r - centre column - and put the manifold's own §9Maintenance Hatch§r into the socket directly below it. Step 9 has the map.
§92.§r §1COOLANT into the chamber's §9COOL§r hatch.§r §9Plain water counts§r - it is the bottom rung of the ladder, and a fan at a few hundred RPM drinks tens of litres a tick, not thousands. Empty your four buckets into it, then run a real water line in behind them. "The Coolant Ladder" is open now and has the rest.
§93.§r §1PROPELLANT into the chamber's §9PROP§r hatch§r, at the other end of the same wall. §9Benzene§r is the honest first rung (§2P x1.25§r). The line stocks all eight injector reserves and the plant lands the timed shot for you. "The Propellant Ladder" is open now too.
§94.§r §9Only then§r run a redstone clock into the Turbine Control Block. About §9one pulse per second§r is the sustainable rate, because that is how fast one slug of steam is produced.

§8How many injectors count as TIMED is simply how many the line kept stocked when the edge arrived - a line that only keeps 5 of 8 runs at 5/8 gain. Hand injection still works, and still has to hit the window.§r

§2§lDONE §lWHEN§r
The Turbine Control Block, the Spiral Cycle Sensor and all §9EIGHT§r Precision Injectors are in your inventory together. §8Steps 4 and 7 paid you four injectors each - that is the eight, and they are the eight this step installs. All of it has to be on you AT ONCE: four now and four later counts as zero.§r
§8This quest only LOOKS at what you are carrying, and it takes nothing. Hold the whole set at once, CLAIM it, and only then break the casings and set the machines into the wall. Already installed them? Wrench them back out for a moment - the check is on your inventory, not on the building.§r
§8The four Water Buckets step 7 paid you are not part of this gate: you pour them into the COOL hatch here, so fill it whenever you like.§r

§5§lCHECK §lYOUR §lWORK§r
The STEAM CHAIN group reads §2Spiral 8/8 injectors§r and its coolant line has stopped saying §cCoolant NOT SUPPLIED§r - it now names the fluid with a live L/t figure. The TURBINE group shows a rising §2RPM§r and a §2cyc/min§r figure, and the §9Spiral Cycle Sensor§r pulses once per ACCEPTED cycle. Use that pulse as your confirmation.
§8Nothing in this step stops the plant either - the reactor runs straight through it.§r

[note]Pulsing faster than steam is produced misses cycles - and a missed cycle still burns the eight litres the line had stocked. If the panel prints a §9HOLD:§r line, read it: it names the exact hatch or the exact reason. The two that stop a NEW plant dead are §cinjectors are dry§r and §ccoolant cannot cover§r, and each of them names the hatch to fill and says the cycle was refused rather than run badly.[/note]

§1WHERE THE POWER LEAVES§r
The output manifold BACK FACE, and nothing else. Nothing is ever built behind it at any tier, so every socket on it looks out at open sky - three courses of four, plus the control column.

[img height=400]btsquests:textures/gui/manifold-face.png[/img]

§5§lDO §lTHIS§r
Put four §9Dynamo Hatches (IV)§r into the four D sockets and run cable off them. Put four §9Energy Hatches (IV)§r into the four E sockets one course above.

  §9EU/t = L/t x spine speed x efficiency x (RPM / 500) x average rotor factor§r

§1WHY ENERGY HATCHES ON A GENERATOR§r
§9They are never a STRUCTURE demand.§r The reactor, the spine, the chamber and the gallery consume nothing - no draw, no idle cost, no start-up cost - so leaving all four E sockets empty can never un-form the plant or stop the campaign, and while any are missing the OUTPUT group prints one grey line counting them.

§cTHEY ARE NOT FURNITURE, THOUGH. TWO MODULES RUN ON THEM.§r
Two of the optional modules on the second blueprint row draw their power through these four sockets and from nowhere else:
  §9Extraction Derrick§r§2 1,920 EU/t§r while it drills
  §9Enrichment Annex§r§2 480 EU/t§r while it enriches
§cBuild either one with no Energy Hatch fitted - or with one fitted and nothing wired into it - and that module silently never turns over.§r So fit at least one §9Energy Hatch (IV)§r here and run a live cable INTO it: your base grid, or straight off one of the Dynamo Hatches in the row below. Both modules running at once is§2 2,400 EU/t§r, which a single IV hatch carries on its own.
§8The panel backs this up: with a module standing and no hatch, that grey line turns RED and names the Derrick and the Annex.§r

§cThe DYNAMOS are the ones that matter.§r Until a Dynamo or a Laser Source sits in that face, everything the turbine makes is thrown away - and the panel says so in as many words: §1Weakest term:§r §2output ceiling 0 (0%)§r §8- fit Dynamo or Laser Source Hatches in the manifold's back face - nothing can leave§r.

§c§lTHE §lTRAP§r
Output is clamped to the SUMMED capacity of the dynamo row and the laser row. Four IV dynamos alone are§c 32,768 EU/t§r - on a tier-5 build that is 0.003% of what the plant is actually making, and the rest is simply thrown away. The panel prints §cCLAMPED from§r when that is happening, and "Break the Clamp" fixes it.

§2§lDONE §lWHEN§r
Four Dynamo Hatches (IV) and four Energy Hatches (IV) are in your inventory together. §8Step 8 paid you the four Energy Hatches.§r
§8This quest only LOOKS at what you are carrying, and it takes nothing. Hold the whole set at once, CLAIM it, and only then break the casings and set the machines into the wall. Already installed them? Wrench them back out for a moment - the check is on your inventory, not on the building.§r

§5§lCHECK §lYOUR §lWORK§r
The OUTPUT group reads §2Generating§r with EU/t leaving, your cables are live, and the grey Energy Hatch line has gone.

ops.desc:
As the materials around you achieve transcendental properties, pistons and gases stop being enough. The answer is gravity: a black hole, held in a cage of mirrors and coils and spun fast enough that its ergosphere can be put to work.

The §9Kerr Ergosphere Engine§r (KEE) holds the hole and does nothing else: it runs no recipes. The machines that use the hole are the §9Kerr modules§r, separate machines standing in the cage's arcs (next quests).

§5§lMAKE §lIT§r The controller is an §9Assembly Line§r recipe: scan a §9Black Hole Seed§r in the Scanner to research it. NEI shows the rest.

§5§lBUILD§r
- Hologram Projector, stack 1: Kerr T1, 76 × 65 × 71. Chunk-load all of it.
- The Black Hole Compressor's own Extreme Density Space-Bending Casing, Hawking Radiation Realignment Focus and Naquadah Alloy frames, plus Beyond the Stars' Superradiant Mirrors, Mirror Backing, Ergosphere Field Coils, Beam Focusing Quadrupoles, Beam Dumps, Harmonic Lining and 232 Bolt Injector Rails. At the hole's height a §9window band§r runs round the drum: one Quantum Glass pane (the outer mirror ring's skin, and the governor arc in front of the hole) with the cells behind it left open, so the hole shows from the front. The optional task is the full bill.
- Hatches: 1 laser or up to 2 energy hatches in the governor arc and 1 to 8 §9bolt buses§r (plain input buses) on the cage. That is all a Kerr needs, at T1 and at T2: no maintenance hatch, and nothing in the 8 §9utility sockets§r beside the bolt buses. The projector builds them as plain shell; a hatch can go there later (a BHC Utility Hatch or a Directive Hatch for redstone, see §cFeeding the Governor§r).
- Hologram markers 7 and 8 show where the two module controllers go.

§5§lRUN§r Everything is in the GUI.
1. Put a §9Black Hole Seed§r in a bolt bus and press Open: the hole opens at§9 8 SM§r (solar masses).
2. It bleeds mass as Hawking radiation,§9 3.2 / M² SM a tick§r. Small holes die fast.
3. The §9governor§r fires bolts from the bolt buses to hold your §9setpoint§r (2-64 SM at T1):
- Neutronium 1/64 SM, Cosmic Neutronium 1/32, Infinity 1/16, Transcendent Metal 1/8, SpaceTime 1/4 SM a bolt;
- at most 4 / 8 / 16 bolts a tick with Mk I / II / III rails. The §llowest§r rail sets the rate, so upgrade them all together.
4. While open, the hole draws§9 8,388,608 EU/t (1 A UEV)§r of containment. Without power the governor stops; below 2 SM the hole evaporates. The power switch does §lnot§r stop the hole.
5. A §9Black Hole Collapser§r in a bolt bus closes it safely: press Collapse twice (with Auto on, a Collapser is used by itself only while the setpoint is 2 SM).
Open and Auto wait for at least§9 1 SM of bolts§r (64 Neutronium bolts) in the bolt buses and§9 1 A UEV§r of containment power: without them the 8 SM hole would evaporate in about 3 s and the Seed would be lost.

[note]Mass sets the modules' bonus: a bigger hole gives more parallels, a smaller one more speed. The controller tooltip has the full block list, and NEI's Multiblock tab previews both tiers.[/note]

[note]HOLD → CLAIM → INSTALL: a retrieval task counts only what is in your inventory, and it never takes the items. So keep the part on you, claim the quest, then place it. Every quest that says HOLD → CLAIM → INSTALL works this way.[/note]

§2§lDONE §lWHEN§r you hold the controller (HOLD → CLAIM → INSTALL).

[note]The Black Hole Compressor's recipe is removed. The KEE has its own Assembly Line recipe (scan a §9Black Hole Seed§r to research it; NEI shows the rest). Every recipe that consumed a BHC controller (the Spacetime Compression Field Generators, the Compressed Circuit Array) now takes a KEE controller instead. A BHC you already placed keeps working.[/note]

So you have made yourself an Eternal DTPF or hopefully a few, and now it is time for the push onwards.

Beyond the Stars replaces TecTech's Eye of Harmony with §9one Eye that grows from T1 to T10§r, a band at a time, with a §9live star§r at its centre. A star is not a batch recipe: it burns every minute, it must be fed, and it must be held steady.

§5§lBUILD§r
- Hologram stack 1 is the T1 core, 102 × 52 × 80. Chunk-load the whole footprint: while any chunk of it is unloaded the Eye is §9frozen§r (nothing runs, nothing is lost). T1 is 102 × 80 blocks, T6 158 × 149, T8 196 × 218, and the controller stands at one end, so a loader on its chunk alone is not enough.
- It is mostly TecTech's own Eye blocks: 9,030 Reinforced Spatial and 4,699 Reinforced Temporal Structure Casings (the Condensate Assembler makes these 32 at a time here), Infinite SpaceTime Energy Boundary Casing, Quantum Glass and the three field generator families. At the star's height the core band's front segments are a §9window§r: one Quantum Glass pane with the cells behind it left open, and later tiers leave an opening in their arms and rim in front of it, so the star shows from the front.
- On the plinth: gas input hatches for Hydrogen and Helium, an input bus for Stellar Ignition Charges, an ME Output Bus, an ME Output Hatch and a maintenance hatch.
- Power is §9wireless EU only§r, and none of it comes back: the Eye makes matter, not power.

§5§lLIGHT §lIT§r Put §9Star Chart: Sol§r in the controller slot (never consumed). Sol lights when:
- a §9Stellar Ignition Charge§r is in a plinth input bus;
- the buffers hold§9 600,000,000 L each of Hydrogen and Helium§r: 10 cycles of upkeep (kept) plus the 100,000,000 L seed cloud (burned);
- the wireless network holds 10 cycles of EU, which the ignition spends.
The protostar contracts for about 40 seconds, then lights.

§5§lRUN§r Every§9 60 s cycle§r Sol burns§9 50,000,000 L Hydrogen + 50,000,000 L Helium§r and§9 1.51 × 10¹¹ EU§r (about 1 A UMV), and makes§9 50,000 L Raw Stellar Plasma§r (NEI: Condensed Raw Stellar Plasma Mixture; the Eye's GUI says Raw Star Matter) into the ME output hatch. Upkeep is paid in full in every zone; a bad zone only cuts the yield.

§5§lAUTOMATE§r Inputs drain into internal buffers every second, so ME stocking input hatches on the gas sockets work. Keep a few charges in the plinth bus from an ME Interface. A dimension display block in the slot runs planets instead (see §cPlanets on the Eye§r).

If a block breaks or every maintenance issue opens, GT switches the Eye off; it switches itself back on once the structure is whole (or the maintenance fixed) and the star relights from a charge. A soft mallet's off stays off.

[warn]§lThe §ltier §lgate:§r Spacetime Compression decides the tier. An Eye of tier N needs every compression generator at tier N or higher. Crude runs T1.[/warn]

[note]The next quests teach the stability field, planets and the road to T2. The controller tooltip and GUI carry every number.[/note]

§2§lDONE §lWHEN§r you hold the controller, Star Chart: Sol and an Ignition Charge (HOLD → CLAIM → INSTALL: a retrieval task counts only what you carry, so claim before you place them).

The §5Primitive§r field generators, tier 2.

In Beyond the Stars the three generator families do three jobs:
- §9Spacetime Compression is the hard gate.§r An Eye of tier N needs every compression generator at tier N or higher. It also decides which planets run.
- §9Time Dilation§r above the star's tier opens the time dial (see §cThe Time Dial§r).
- §9Stabilisation§r calms the star: noise and events shrink 5 % per tier above the first.

The families mix freely, and the §llowest§r of each family counts. The hologram places compression at the trigger stack's tier and never downgrades a generator already placed.

§5§lTIER §lSTEP§r You do not re-craft. In the §9Condensate Assembler§r a generator of the tier below plus only what the new tier adds (NEI shows it) becomes the next tier: its Kerr controller, casing and singularity cells stay inside. A §9Stabilisation§r generator takes one §9Spacetime Compression§r and one §9Time Dilation Retrofit Kit§r of the new tier (built on a Retrofit Frame from the same parts) for the two generators it holds. Same time as a fresh craft, only cheaper.

§5§lCIRCUITS§r Every generator takes UXV circuits, more at each tier. Any UXV circuit fits; from Eye T4 the §9Empyrean Mainframe§r is the far cheaper one (see §cEmpyrean Circuits§r).

Primitive lets your Eye reach §9T2 (Sirius A).§r

The §5Stable§r field generators, tier 3.

How the three generator families gate the Eye, and how a generator steps up a tier, is on §cT2: Primitive§r (Tier 12 - UMV).

Stable gates §9T3 (Arcturus).§r

The §5Advanced§r field generators, tier 4.

How the three generator families gate the Eye, and how a generator steps up a tier, is on §cT2: Primitive§r (Tier 12 - UMV).

Advanced gates §9T4 (the neutron star):§r the Core Collapse will not start without it.

The neutron star's harvest, 3.6864 L for every litre of Hyperdense Stellar Mixture fed: the first matter that does not come from a living star.

It feeds Sirius B at UXV (18,432 L a batch), the magnetar merger, and Reinforced Components here. As Entangled White Dwarf Matter it goes into the T5 and T6 cores.

[note]The T4 → T5 milestones: §l147,456 §lL§r made from cycles that were never worse than Stable, §l4 §lh §lResonant§r, and one §lDeep §lDark §lrun§r on this Eye.[/note]

We hope you enjoy your stay, though be prepared for a lot of waiting.

In Beyond the Stars this is the Eye's second half: §9Sirius B (T5)§r cools white dwarfs into black, and §9the magnetar (T6)§r runs on Antipolarization Agent. Then the §9Quasar Engine§r: its bursts hold the first galaxies, §9Triangulum (T7)§r and §9the Milky Way (T8),§r and power your base. The crafted Stargate has moved to §1The Endgame§r, after MAX.

[warn]§lUniversium§r comes with Eye T10 (coming later). Nothing Beyond the Stars asks for needs it: the Eye's cores, the Homogeny Tier II Core and every Quasar, Conduit and Supermassive Lattice part take twice as many UMV parts in place of the pack's UXV Field Generator, Sensor and Emitter. The pack's own UXV parts (UXV components, the UXV CoAL, the UXV Field Generator) still need MHDCSM and Universium, so they wait for Eye T10. UXV circuits are craftable: the Quantum circuit needs no Universium, and from Eye T4 the far cheaper §9Empyrean Mainframe§r fills any UXV circuit slot.[/warn]

Sirius B's harvest, made batch by batch: 4,608 L × the batch's mean yield.

It goes into Refined Components, the Magnetar Seed Core (as its condensate), the merger that spawns the magnetar (4,608 L) and the magnetar's reserve top-ups (450 L at a time).
